## Overview

The `lrmodel` package was designed to re-implement the base R functions `lm()` 
and `summary()` for linear regression models. The functions in this package
generate and summarize results from a linear regression model. This vignette 
demonstrates how to use the package's two core functions, `lrmodel()` and  
`lrmodel_summary()`, to fit a linear regression model and explore the results. 
It also includes a comparison of the correctness and efficiency of `lrmodel()` 
and `lrmodel_summary()` vs. the base R functions `lm()` and `summary()` using 
`all.equal()` and `bench::mark()`.

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>"
)
```

```{r setup}
library(lrmodel)
```

## Example

The `penguins` dataset is a built-in R dataset containing measurements of adult penguins in Antarctica. We can use this dataset to explore whether penguin body mass is predicted by flipper length and sex, leveraging the functions in the `lrmodel` package.

First, let's fit a linear regression model to the `penguins` dataset:

```{r}
penguins_model <- lrmodel(
  body_mass ~ flipper_len + sex, 
  data = penguins
)
penguins_model
```

We can interpret the coefficient estimates generated by the model. For example, the model predicts that a 1 mm increase in flipper length is associated with a 47 gram increase in body mass, holding sex constant.

We can also plot the relationship between flipper length, sex, and body mass as predicted by the model:

```{r, fig.width=7, fig.height=5, out.width="100%"}
plot(
  x = penguins_model$model$flipper_len, y = penguins_model$fitted.values,
  col = c("blue", "green")[penguins_model$model$sex],
  pch = 16,
  xlab = "Flipper Length (mm)",
  ylab = "Fitted Values"
)
legend(
  "bottomright", 
  legend = c("Female", "Male"), 
  col = c("blue", "green"), 
  pch = 16,
  title = "Sex"
)
```

To view a formatted summary of our linear model results, we can use the function `lrmodel_summary()`:

```{r}
penguins_summary <- lrmodel_summary(penguins_model)
penguins_summary
```

From this summary, we can see that flipper length and sex are both highly significant predictors of penguin body mass (p < 0.001).

We can also view the R-squared and adjusted R-squared values for the model:

```{r}
penguins_summary$r.squared
penguins_summary$adj.r.squared
```

Our linear regression model with flipper length and sex explains 80.6% of the variation in penguin body mass.

Lastly, we can view the number of observations that were deleted from our model due to missing information:

```{r}
penguins_summary$n_obs_del
```

There were 11 total observations deleted from our model.

## Correctness

The correctness of the `lrmodel()` and `lrmodel_summary()` functions is 
demonstrated below by comparing the output of each function to the base R 
functions `lm()` and `summary()` using `all.equal()`.

```{r}
all.equal(
  lrmodel(mpg ~ wt, mtcars)$coefficients, 
  lm(mpg ~ wt, mtcars)$coefficients
)

all.equal(
  lrmodel(mpg ~ wt, mtcars)$residuals,
  lm(mpg ~ wt, mtcars)$residuals
)

all.equal(
  lrmodel(mpg ~ wt, mtcars)$fitted.values,
  lm(mpg ~ wt, mtcars)$fitted.values
)

all.equal(
  lrmodel_summary(lrmodel(mpg ~ wt, mtcars))$residuals,
  summary(lm(mpg ~ wt, mtcars))$residuals
)

all.equal(
  lrmodel_summary(lrmodel(mpg ~ wt, mtcars))$sigma,
  summary(lm(mpg ~ wt, mtcars))$sigma
)

all.equal(
  lrmodel_summary(lrmodel(mpg ~ wt, mtcars))$r.squared,
  summary(lm(mpg ~ wt, mtcars))$r.squared
)
```

## Efficiency

The efficiency of `lrmodel()` and `lrmodel_summary()` vs. the base R functions
is demonstrated below using `bench::mark()`.

```{r}
result <- bench::mark(
  lrmodel(mpg ~ wt, mtcars)$coefficients,
  lm(mpg ~ wt, mtcars)$coefficients
)
```

```{r, fig.width=7, fig.height=5, out.width="100%"}
result
plot(result)
```

```{r}
result <- bench::mark(
  lrmodel(mpg ~ wt, mtcars)$residuals,
  lm(mpg ~ wt, mtcars)$residuals
)
```

```{r, fig.width=7, fig.height=5, out.width="100%"}
result
plot(result)
```

```{r}
result <- bench::mark(
  lrmodel(mpg ~ wt, mtcars)$fitted.values,
  lm(mpg ~ wt, mtcars)$fitted.values
)
```

```{r, fig.width=7, fig.height=5, out.width="100%"}
result
plot(result)
```

```{r}
result <- bench::mark(
  lrmodel_summary(lrmodel(mpg ~ wt, mtcars))$residuals,
  summary(lm(mpg ~ wt, mtcars))$residuals
)
```

```{r, fig.width=7, fig.height=5, out.width="100%"}
result
plot(result)
```

```{r}
result <- bench::mark(
  lrmodel_summary(lrmodel(mpg ~ wt, mtcars))$adj.r.squared,
  summary(lm(mpg ~ wt, mtcars))$adj.r.squared
)
```

```{r, fig.width=7, fig.height=5, out.width="100%"}
result
plot(result)
```
